newsitem.title: CHINA: HK MANUFACTURERS SEE ORDERS UP IN 97 H2 - POLL.
newsitem.headline: HK MANUFACTURERS SEE ORDERS UP IN 97 H2 - POLL.

text.p: Hong Kong manufacturers expect a slight increase in volume of orders in the second half of 1997 compared with the same period in 1996, a government survey showed on Thursday.

The half-yearly survey conducted by the Census and Statistic Department found manufacturers in the electronic and electrical products, the electrical machinery and the printing industries generally expect a moderate increase in volume of orders.
Manufacturers in the wearing apparel and the fabricated metal products industries anticipated a fairly stable volume of orders, while textile manufacturers expected a decrease in volume of orders.

In general, manufacturers expected capacity utilisation to remain stable in the second half of 1997 compared with the first half. However, profit margins were expected to be lowered over the same period.
The survey is held on a half-yearly basis, covering about 300 firms from major manufacturing industries -- the import/export trades, the banking industry and the construction sectors.

It collects views of firms on the short-term prospects of the various major business sectors covered and aims at providing a quick reference for assessing the short-term future economic performance of Hong Kong.
